text: A spiall priviledge graunted to Samurt MAson and his assignes, for 14 yeares next ensuing, within England, Ireland, and Wales, to use and practise the way and invenéon of the sole making and dying of buckromes and tillits in whole peeces, with a prohibiéon to all others to use the same— yeilding yearely to the Crowne 23/64 for every dozen peeces of buckrome or tillitts (none of the said peeces exceeding the length of sixe yards); with the ordinary proviso to make this graunt voide if it be founde piudiciall to the comonwealth. Teste apud West', xviij® May, anno pa. p bre &*.

A grant unto Thomas Berry, his execrs, admrs, & assigns, of the sole use & benefit of his new invencon of curing the sweepings of ships, and thereby rendring the same usefull and saleable, which otherwise would be of little or no value, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for and during the term of fourteen years according to the statute in such case made and provided. Teste I£ apd Westm, 18° die Febry, anno pd. p bre, &c.

A grant unto William Wood, esq1', his execrs, admrs, and assignes, of the sole use and benefit of his new invencon to make raw iron or iron metal, Spared in an air furnace with pit coal, [mediately from iron stone, iron mine, or iron ore, being different from and much better and finer than sow or pig iron ; to hold the same within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon- Tweed for and during the term of 14 years according to the statute in such case made and provided. Teste ty apd Westm, 18° die Septembris, anno pd. p bre, &c.

A grant unto John Allen, dr in physick, his extors, admrs, & assignes, of the sole use & benefit of his invencon of a new method of heating and boyling water and other liquors with far less expense than by any method now in use, which will be of great service in working of engines for raising of water by fire, and also in brewing, distilling, and all other uses where great fires are required ; and also of his new invencon for the application of certain powers to give mocon to engines, whereby a ship may be navigated in a calm, from whence innumerable advantages will accrew in sailing and be a great preservation to His Majtie's subjects in engagements at sea, and will be also of great use in draining of mines and for performing of other great works where force is required ; and likewise of his new method to dry malt with any sort of fuel, whereby the malt will be rendered sweeter and the beer brewed therewith will be much more pleasant and wholesome ; to hold and exercise the same within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for and during the term of 14 years according to the statute in such case made and provided. Teste, &c, ut ult. p bre, &c.

A grant unto George Kettle, his extors, admvs, & assignes, of the sole use and benefit of his new invencon, way, or method for making or dying men or women's black hatts with white or any other coloured ruffs, which by the comon methods of making hatts with ruffs are only black; to hold & exercise the same, &c (ut supra). Teste R, &c, ut ult°. p bre, &c.

A grant unto Georoe Reynoldson, of the parish of S1 Helen's, in the city of York, upholsterer, his extors, admors, and assigns, of the sole use and benefit of his new invencons of a machine that gives exactly the way a ship makes and counts her lee way, that tells what speed the winds blow, and proves the different force of current in any depth ; and also of a machine that will retard a ship's driving upon a lee shore where there is no anchorage, or being forced back in her voyage by contrary winds ; to hold and exercise the same within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for and during the term of 14 years according to the statute in such case made and pvided. Teste I£ apd Westm, 18° die Octobris, anno pit. p bre, &c.

A grant unto Walter Churchman, citizen of Bristol, his exors, admrs, and assignes, of the sole use and benefit of his new invencon of a machine or engine to be moved or worked by the united powers of weight and draught for raising water for any uses, and for draining of low lands, coal pits, and mines, and for grinding, stamping, and all other works wherein all or any of the mechanical powers are or may be applied ; to hold and exercise the same within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for and during the term of 14 years according to the statute in such case made and pvided ; and a clause is inserted for obliging him particularly to describe and ascertain the nature of his said invention, by an instrument under his hand and sealed, to be inrolled in the High Court of Chancery within two calendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Maj*y at Westm, the 21st day of March, in the said year. By writt, &c.

A grant unto John Tull, his execrs, admrs, & assignes, for his invencon of a new sedan chair fixed upon a wheel carriage and springs, to be drawn by horses, and to carry one, two, or more persons one hundred miles a day with much more ease and safety than any carriage now in use; to hold and exercise the same within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon- Tweed for and during the term of 14 years according to the statute in such case made and provided ; and a clause is inserted for obliging him, by an instrument in writing under his hand & seal, to be inrolled in the High Court of Chancery within three kalendar months from the date hereof, particularly to describe and ascertain the nature of his said invention. Witness His Matie at Westmr, the 13th day of May, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto Roger Pleunius, of the parish of Sl George Hanover Square, in the liberty of Westm1, harpsichord maker, of his new invencon of meliorating the musical instruments called harpsichords, lyrichords (which are harpsichords strung with cat gut), and spinnets; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, & assignes, for the term of 14 years, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed pursuant to the Act of Parliament in that behalf. Witness His Matie at Westm1", the 30th day of December, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto Lewis Pantin, of the parish of S1 Ann, within the liberty of the city of Westm1', in the county of Middx, goldsmith, of his new invented engine for raising & taking up ballast from the bottom of rivers & other purposes therein menconed; to hold to him, his execrs, admrs, & assignes for the term of 14 years, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed pursuant to the statute in that behalf ; and a clause is inserted obliging him particularly to describe and ascertain the nature of his said invencon, by an instrument in writing under his hand & seal, to be inrolled in the High Court of Chancery within four kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westmr, the 21st day of January, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto Thomas Hawkes, of Wells, in the county of Norfolk, of his new invencon whereby riding in a chaise, chair, or such like vehicle is rendred much more safe & easy to our subjects than by any other way yet made use of ; to hold to him, his exec1"8, admrs, & assignes, for the term of 14 years, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, pursuant to the startute in that behalf; and a clause is inserted obliging him particularly to describe the nature of his said invencon, by an instrument in writing under his hand & seal, to be inrolled in the High Court of Chancery within four kalendar months from the date hereof. Witness His Matie at Westmr, the 26th day of July, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto Isaac Moore, of Queen Street, Upper Moorfields, and William Pine, of the city of Bristol, letter founders, printers, and partners, of their new invented method of casting cases in metal for holding and containing metallic letters or printing types of .a peculiar construction, to fix in the said cases, for marking or printing on silk, muslin, linnen, woollen, leather, paper, parchment, and vellum, together with raised letters for signs, monumental inscriptions, and other purposes ; and also new invented printing presses, the plattens whereof are made of iron and other metals, as well as wood, and are suspended and counteracted by a ballanceor weight ; to hold to them, their exors, admors, and asss, within England, Wales, the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and all the colonies and plantations abroad, for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westm1", the 6th day of Nov1", in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Isaac Whitehouse, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, enameller, of his new invented method of making coat buttons, breast buttons, sleeve buttons, vest and other buttons, studs, bracelets, necklaces, lockets, rings, watch chains, boxes, and trinkets ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwickupon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westm1', the 31st day of August, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Joseph Hateley, of Dudley, in the county of Worcester, engineer, of his new invented rotatory reciprocal fire engine, for saving of fuel, increasing the powers, reducing the expence, and making them of more utility and general good than any heretofore discovered, for lifting, raising or forcing of water, raising or drawing of coal, iron, stone, clay, lead, tin, copper, and for the completion of business in all manufactures where mechanic powers are necessary, or any other business that can be performed by animate or inanimate powers whatever; to hold to him, his exors, admo , and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westminster, the third day of August, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Stedman, of the parish of Saint Ann's, Soho, in the county of Middlesex, jeweller, of his new invented simpathetic hinges and quadrants, with folding doors, gates, and shutters, with new invented fastnings for the same ; to hold to him, his executors, administrators, and assigns, within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to* the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westminster, the 17th day of November, in the year above. By writt, &c.

A grant unto Watrer Tayror, of the town and county of Southampton, blockmaker, and Wimt1am Coxuins, of the parish of Saint | Mary, Lambeth, in the county of Surry, engine maker, of their new invented improvement in the construction of pumps, the chambers, pistons, and boxes thereunto belonging, so as to prevent their being choak’d with gravel, sand, and filth on ship board, and for raising water with less power than those now Fan use; to hold to them, their ecXors, admors, & ass’, within England, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 y' pursuant to the statute; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at West", the 19" day of Sept', in the year above. By writ, &°

A grant unto RaLtpH Gout, of the parish of Saint Luke, in the 1789. | county of Middlesex, watchmaker, of his new invented machinery, for the purpose of measuring distance, and which will not only ascertain, with the greatest precision, the number of miles a person travels, but will also afford security to the passenger in a carriage and preserve the body thereof from injury, in case either of the springs, or any part to which they are attached, should break or give way; to hold to him, his eXors, adfiors, & ass’, within Eng“, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 y's, pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at West", the 7" day of November, in the year above. : By writ, &°.

A grant unto Samuel Young Hunclass, of Lambeth Marsh, in the parish of Saint Mary, Lambeth, in the co. of Surry, painter, of his new invented method of making & rendering elastic and water proof all sorts of painted, printed, varnished, or japanned linnen, cotton, woollen cloths, stuff, or silk, or any other material interwoven therewith; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & asss, within Engd, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and also within His Majesty's colonies and plantations abroad, for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at West1", the 15th Janry, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Samuel Peal, of Wirksworth, in the county of Derby, cordwainer, of his new improved method of making & rendering perfectly water proof all kinds of leather, cotton, linen and woollen cloths, silks, stuffs, paper, wood, and other manufactures and substances, for the purpose of being worked up into shoes, boots, and other wearing apparel, and to be used on all occasions where dryness or a power of repelling wet or moisture may be required ; to hold to him, his exors, adffiors, and ass", within England, Wales, and town of Berwick-upon-Tweed, and also within His Majesty's colonies and plantations abroad, for the term of 14yrs pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within four calendar months from the date hereof. W. H. M. at Westr, the 2d day of May, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Francis Noble Knipe, of Devonshire Street, Queen Square, gentleman, of his new invented machine for raising or dispersing water, condensing air, or other purposes, possessing a self assisting power, effected by the pressure of the column of air, water, or resistance in any direction upon the forcing power, in favour of the agent or working power in the proportion of about seven to thirteen and upwards, according to the different modifications of the machine, which admits of a great variety of changes, and hath no similarity or likeness in principle to any engine hitherto made use of, is adapted to all situations and purposes of raising water, is more simple, compact, and portable, less expensive, and by far more effectual, than any hydraulic engine now in being ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, & asss, within Engd, Wales, & town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of 14 years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inrol the same within one calendar month from the date hereof. W. H. M. at West1", the 7th day of July, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Michael Logan, of Paradise Street, in the parish of S* Mary, Rotherhithe, in the county of Surry, engineer, for his new invented centrifugal barrel engine of central force, for raising water and great weights from great depths, and applicable to all manufactories or systems of machinery, either great or small, requiring the action of circular motion, such as an effectual power in mill work, water works, and clock work ; to hold to him, his exors, adniors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westm1, the 8th day of March, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Williams and Joseph Williams, of Holywell Street, in the parish of Sl Clement Danes, in the liberty of Westminster, stationers, for their new invented method of binding all sorts of books ; to hold to them, their exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westm1", the 4th day of Nov1", in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Fitzgerald, esq1*, of Grays Inn, in the county of Middlesex, for his new invented mathematical instrument, to be called "the marine level," the properties of which are to show every deviation from the horizontal plane of ships and vessels ; and which is also applicable to various purposes in surveying, levelling, and ascertaining vertical and perpendicular situations ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the 1 1th day of Aug1, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Todd, of Bolton, in the county of Lancaster, cotton spinner, for his new invented method of weaving and manufacturing woollen, cotton, linen, silk, and worsted cloths or stuffs, and also certain improvements on and additions to the machines used in weaving, by means of looms wrought by water, steam engines, horses, or any other power ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within England, Wales, and the town of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within one calendar month from the date thereof. W. H. M. at Westmr, the 14th day of April, in the year above. By writ, &c.

A grant unto John Barton, of the town of Tunbridge, in the county of Kent, gentleman, for his invented machine for raising weights or water with greater facility and at less expence than any at present used ; to hold to him, his exors, admors, and assigns, within that part of our united kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland called England, our dominion of Wales, and towm of Berwick-upon-Tweed for the term of fourteen years pursuant to the statute ; with a clause to inroll the same within two calendar months from the date thereof. B7 writ, &c.

A grant unto John Malzel, of Poland Street, in the coy of Middx, machinist, for his invented instrument or instruments, machine or machines, for the improvement or improvements of all musical performance, which he denominates a metronome or musical time keeper ; to hold, &c ; 6 months to inroll. By writ, &c.

A grant unto James Jeffray, of Glasgow^, in that part of the united kingdom called Scotland, professor of anatomy in the University of Glasgow, for his invented " Certain combinations of and improvements in machinery to be moved by wind, steam, animal strength, water, or other power, by means of which boats, barges, ships, or other floating vessels may be propelled or moved in water, and which invention is further applicable to other useful purposes" ; to hold, &c; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Bainbridge, of Holborn, in the city of London, musician and turner, for his "Invented certain improvements in the double and single flageolet or English flute"; to hold, &c; 2 months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto GrorGEe Smarr, of Pedlars Acre, Lambeth, in the county of Surrey, civil engineer, for his invit “ Improvement in the manufacture of chains, which he denominates ‘mathematical chains’”; to hold, &«; six months. . By writ, &*.

A grant unto Benjamin Cook, of Birmingham, in the coy of Warwick, brass founder, for his invented " Certain imprts in making or constructing hinges of various descriptions"; to hold, &c ; six mos. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Charles Whitlaw, of N° 13, Bayswater Terrace, Paddington, in the county of Middx, medical botanist, for his invented "Improvement or improvements in administering medicines by the agency of steam or vapour"; to hold, &r ; six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto William Robinson, of Craven Street, Strand, in the county of Middlesex, esq., for his invented or found out " A new method of propelling vessels by steam on canals or navigable rivers, by means of a moveable apparatus attached to the stem or stern of the vessel "; to hold, &c; two months. By writ, &<\

A grant unto Goldsworthy Gurney, of Argyle Street, Hanover Square, in the county of Middlesex, surgeon, for his invented " Certain improvements in locomotive engines and the apparatus connected therewith "; six months. By writ, &c.
A grant unto Neil Arnott, of Bedford Square, in the county of Middlesex, esqre, for his invention of " Certain improvements on metallic pens and on pen holders "; six months. By writ, &c,
A grant unto Thomas Horne, of Aston, near Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, brass founder, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the manufacture of hinges six months. By writ, &c.

A grant unto Charles Wheatstone, of Conduit Street, in the county of Middlesex, musical instrument manufacturer, and John Green, of Soho Square, in the same county, musical instrument manufacturer, for their invention of " A new methed or methods of forming musical instruments in which continuous sounds are produced from strings, wires, or springs": 6 months.

A grant unto Thomas Bradshaw Whitfield, of New Street Square* in the county of Middlesex, lamp manufacturer, for his invention of "Improvements in producing parallel motion to the piston rods of pumps for lamps and other purposes ; which improvements are also applicable to machinery in general where parallel motion is required"; 6 months.

A grant unto Frederic Edouard Fraissinet, of Covent Garden Square, in the city of Westminster, for " Certain improvements in the machinery for propelling vessels by steam, by which their speed will be much accelerated, with a diminished power and with a diminished action in the water"; being a communication from a foreigner residing abroad" ; 6 months.

A grant unto John Hughes Rees, of Penymaes, near Llanelly, in the county of Carmarthen, esquire, for " Certain improvements in the machinery applicable to the raising of water for propelling boats, carriages, and other machinery"; being a communication from a foreigner residing abroad ; 6 months.

A grant unto GrorcEe Smirn, of the Navy Club House, Bond Street, in the county of Middlesex, a captain in the royal navy, for his invention of ‘Certain improvements in vessels to be propelled by steam or other power, and in the construction and arrangement of the machinery for propelling ”; 6 months.

A grant unto WiL1t1AM PontTiIFEX, of Shoe Lane, in the city of Lon< don, coppersmith, for his invention of “ Improvements in apparatus and materials employed in filtering and clarifying waters and other liquids”; 6 months.

A grant unto James Bingham, of Sheffield, in the county of York, manufacturer, and John Amort Boden, of the same place, manufacturer, for " Certain improved compositions which are made to resemble ivory, bone, horn, mother of pearl, and other substances applicable to the manufacture of handl< a of knives, forks, and razors, pianoforte keys, snuff boxes, and various other articles month-.

A grant unto Wilkinson Steele and Patrick Sanderson Steele, manufacturing and furnishing ironmongers, George Street, Edinburgh, for their invention of " Improvements in kitchen ranges for culinary purposes, and apparatus for raising the temperature of water for baths and other uses"; 6 months.
A grant unto Daniel Gooch, of Paddington Green, in the county of Middlesex, engineer, for his invention of " Certain improvements in wheels and locomotive engines to be used on railways"; 6 months.

A grant unto James Bingham, of Sheffield, in the county of York, manufacturer, for his invention of " Certain improved compositions which are made to resemble ivory, bone, mother of pearl, and other substances, applicable to the manufacture of handles of knives, forks, and razors, pianoforte keys, snuff boxes, and various other articles " ; 6 months.

A grant unto Andrew Smith, of Belper, in the county of Derby' engineer, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the arrangement and construction of engines to be worked by the force of steam or other fluids, which improved engines are also applicable to the raising of water and other liquids "; six months.

A grant unto Joseph Ratcliff, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, manufacturer, for " Certain improvements in the construction and manufacture of hinges for hanging and closing doors"; being a communication ; six months.

A grant unto Henri Alriionse Bounevialle Bouveiron, of Bordeaux, in the kingdom of France, now of Trevor Square, in the county of Middlesex, merchant, for " Improvements in axletrees"; 6 months ; being a communication.

A grant unto Josiaii Longmore, of Regent Street, Kennington, in the county of Surrey, silversmith, for his invention of " Certain improvements in pens, penholders, and pencil cases ; part of which improvements are applicable to other useful purposes"; 6 months.

A grant unto John Hinks, George Wells, and Joseph Finnemore, all of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, metallic pen makers, for their invention of " Improvements in the manufacture of metallic pens, and in machines for manufacturing metallic pens"; 6 months.

A grant unto Henry Davies, of Norbury, in the county of Stafford, engineer, for his invention of "Certain improvements in the construction of vessels for conveying goods or passengers on water ; also certain improved arrangements of machinery for communicating motion to such vessels"; 6 months.

A grant unto William Taylor, of Birmingham, in the county of Warwick, door -spring manufacturer, for his invention of " Improvements in the manufacture of axle pullies, and in pegs or pins for hanging hats or other garments thereon "; 6 months.
A gi ant unto Samuel Wilkes, of Wolverhampton, in the county of Stafford, iron founder, for his invention of "Improvements in the manufacture of hinges"; 6 months.
A grant unto Josiah Wilkinson, of Lincoln's Inn Fields, in the county of Middlesex, gentleman, for "Certain improvements in filtering water and other fluids"; being a communication ; 6 months.

A grant unto Charles Tetlev, of Bradford, in the West Riding of the county of York, stock and share broker, for his invention of " Certain improvements in machinery for raising and impelling water and other liquids, and also thereby to obtain mechanical power"; 6 months.

A grant unto Stephen Perry, of Woodland Place, St. John's Wood, gentleman, for his invention of " Certain improvements in the manufacture of rings, straps, bands and bandages, cords and string, and in their application to clockwork, to locks and other fastenings, to presses, to books, to paperholders, to candle lamps, to window sashes, to doors, to window blinds, to seals and surfaces for lying and reclining upon"; 6 months.
A grant unto Thomas Yates, of Preston, in the county of Lancaster, watchmaker, for his invention of " Improvements in time-keepers"; 6 months.

A grant unto Anthony Bernhard Von Rathen, of Putney, in the county of Surrey, civil engineer, for his invention of " Certain universal wheels or improved direct rotatory engines, to be worked by steam, air, or any other elastic power "; 6 months.

A grant unto William Martin, of Saint Pierre les Calais, in the republic of France, mechanist, for his invention of " Certain improvements in machinery for figuring textile fabrics ; parts of which improvements are applicable to playing certain musical instruments, and also to printing and other like purposes "; 6 months.
A grant unto James Forster, of Liverpool, merchant, for his invention of " Improvements in filtering water and other liquids "; 6 months.
